main_body: Timber-frame farmhouse: a large red-tile roof slope with a half-timbered dormer above a cream plaster front wall with a big double barn door and two small windows
top_band: Roof slope: ridge cap rows 0-2 (dark brown), a cream ridge-tile highlight on rows 3-4, then orange/maroon tile rows 5-53 (L about 60-86). The lowest tile row (53) is lighter, then a dark eave shadow on rows 54-55.
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened slope seen from above, with a ridge highlight, a tile-edge row and a dark 2-row eave shadow before the plaster wall. The wall below has its own front face, with timber framing, an inset door and windows with dark frames. The dormer sits on the roof slope with its own sill. It matches the house references, where a roof slope sits above the front wall, so it reads as a 3/4 building and not a flat elevation. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof tiles use about 5 tones (cream highlight, orange, red, maroon, deep purple) with a per-tile pattern. The plaster has speckle, the wood is shaded in several browns, and the door has planks, diagonal braces and studs. Outlines are tinted dark brown or maroon (1% neutral). Median 21 colours per tile, above the references (18 and 11); 0% flat fill. The tile pattern is somewhat regular but as rich as the references.
